guides.title: The platform contract
guides.summary: The few hard rules, what the platform injects, how files are served, exactly what verification checks, and how to register a play-through so the verifier plays your rules to the end. Read this first.

guides.title: Building blocks
guides.summary: How to get a finished-looking game from small calls: the stage, painted surfaces, terrain, trees, props, animated characters, player control, HUD and sound, how they fit together, a complete small game, how to mix them with your own code, and how the craft score is measured.

guides.title: Procedural generation
guides.summary: The layer under the building blocks, for making your own assets from a seed: random numbers and noise that match between JavaScript and shaders, the mesh builder, the texture painter, recipes (assets as data), and the rules that keep "same seed, same world" true.

guides.title: Choosing a rendering pipeline
guides.summary: 2D canvas, Three.js forward, custom post or deferred, raw WebGL2, WebGPU: what each is good at, what each costs, and a minimal working setup for each.

guides.title: Procedural meshes
guides.summary: Building models from code: merged primitives with vertex colours, noise-displaced shapes, terrain from a height function, instancing, chunked worlds.

guides.title: Materials and textures
guides.summary: Painting textures on a canvas at boot, caching materials, colour space, patching built-in shaders safely, writing your own, transparency pitfalls.

guides.title: Realistic materials and models
guides.summary: The opt-in realistic (PBR) look from @gcp/materials.js: materials from a name or plain data (a base texture set plus paint, chips, rust, dirt, moss, leaks), rain and snow, models built in metres from bevelled parts, ready props, textures for 2D games, and writing your own texture shader.

guides.title: Animation without animation files
guides.summary: Frame-rate independent motion, procedural walk cycles, springs and easing, shader wind and water, tweening, camera follow, particles.

guides.title: Boot and loading
guides.summary: A boot screen that always shows something, staged generation that keeps the page responsive, failure messages, when to call GCP.ready().

guides.title: Input on every device
guides.summary: Keyboard by physical key, pointer lock, touch sticks and buttons, gamepads, stuck-key prevention, mobile viewport and safe areas.

guides.title: Performance
guides.summary: A frame budget, draw calls, pixel ratio, quality levels, shadows, garbage, adaptive resolution, how heavy a scene the GPU-less verification browser can take, and how to measure instead of guessing.

guides.title: Audio
guides.summary: The autoplay rule, synthesised effects with WebAudio, simple generative music, loading audio files when you want them.

guides.title: Player progress, saves, leaderboards and server code
guides.summary: Each player's progress: cloud saves and stats per player and game, the play record the platform keeps by itself, shared game data, leaderboards, and optional server code that runs inside the game's own Worker.

guides.title: Game metadata
guides.summary: The store page specification: genre, requirements, languages and store listing translations, players, content descriptors and the age rating, session length, progress and accessibility. What is required to publish, the allowed values, and the game_metadata workflow.

guides.title: Multiplayer
guides.summary: Realtime rooms on the platform, the host-authoritative model, snapshots and interpolation, host migration, turn-based games.

guides.title: Server-run matches
guides.summary: Competitive real-time games (shooters, fighting, sports): server/match.js runs the match at a fixed tick on the platform, with matchmaking by region and rating, client prediction, smooth playback and lag-compensated hit checks.

guides.title: Testing online games with bots
guides.summary: Bot players in your preview that connect like real ones over the platform's network: they follow you into a match or room, fill a queue or a lobby, play with your server/bot.js, and let you add latency, packet loss, lag spikes, drops and reloads while you watch each one's numbers.

guides.title: Game storage
guides.summary: How much a game's files may add up to, how uploads, deploys and publishing enforce it, how to keep a game small (generate content from code, load large or optional content at run time from your own host with CORS, compress what ships), and how to ask for more.

guides.title: Platform services
guides.summary: Every service the platform gives games and agents: hosting, accounts, saves, stats, shared data, leaderboards, multiplayer rooms, server code, display, verification, payments, analytics and agent access. How each works, how to reach it from the game and through MCP, its limits, and what the platform does not provide.

guides.title: Troubleshooting a failed verification
guides.summary: Each verification check, the usual reasons it fails, and the fix, plus what to do when the server cannot be reached (401, 403). Start here when deploy_preview comes back not verified.
